lesson.d: a time when a teacher helps you learn something
lesson.ex: Our science lesson is on Monday.

animal.d: a living thing that can move, like a dog or a bird
animal.ex: My favorite animal is a dog.

grow.ex: My little sister grows so fast!

look.d: to use your eyes to see something
look.ex: Look at the bird in the tree!

wonder.d: to ask yourself a question in your head
wonder.ex: I wonder why the sky is blue.

baby.d: a very young child or animal

different.ex: The two cats are different colors.

parent.ex: My parents take me to school.

explore.d: to look around a new place to learn about it
explore.ex: We explore the woods with Dad.

inquiry.d: a question that you try to find the answer to
inquiry.ex: Our class did an inquiry about bugs.

activity.d: something you do, like a game or a job

alike.d: the same or almost the same

thing.ex: Put your things in your bag.

compare.d: to look at how things are the same and different

venn_diagram.d: two circles that cross, to show what is the same and what is different
venn_diagram.ex: We used a Venn diagram to compare cats and dogs.

tiger.d: a big wild cat with orange fur and black stripes

read.d: to look at words and understand them
read.ex: I read a book before bed.

learn.d: to get to know something new
learn.ex: I learn to ride a bike.

essential.ex: Water is essential for every living thing.

question.d: something you ask to find out an answer

life_cycle.d: how a living thing starts life, grows, has young and dies
life_cycle.ex: A frog has an interesting life cycle.

vocabulary.d: the words you know or learn
vocabulary.ex: We learn new vocabulary every week.

larva.d: the young stage of an insect after it comes out of the egg, like a caterpillar

pupa.d: the stage when an insect rests inside a hard case and changes
pupa.ex: The pupa hangs from a branch.

insect.d: a small animal with six legs, like an ant or a bee

bird.d: an animal with feathers and wings
bird.ex: A bird sings in the tree.

fish.d: an animal that lives and swims in water
fish.ex: The fish swims in the pond.

reptile.d: an animal with dry, scaly skin, like a snake or a lizard

amphibian.d: an animal that lives in water and on land, like a frog

lay.d: to make an egg come out of the body

egg.d: a round thing that some baby animals grow in
egg.ex: The bird has three eggs in its nest.

mammal.d: an animal with hair or fur that drinks milk from its mother when it is young

birth.ex: Our cat gave birth to four kittens.

live_adj.ex: Mammals give birth to live babies.

chicken.d: a farm bird that lays eggs
chicken.ex: The chicken lives on a farm.

life.d: the time when someone is alive, from being born to dying
life.ex: My grandma had a long, happy life.

die.ex: The flower died because it had no water.

panda.d: a black and white bear from China that eats bamboo

inside.ex: The cat is inside the box.

body.d: all of a person or an animal, from head to feet
body.ex: Exercise is good for your body.

drink.d: to take water or milk into your mouth and swallow

milk.d: a white drink that comes from mothers and cows

chick.ex: The chick is small and yellow.

break.d: to make something come apart into pieces

shell.d: a hard cover on the outside of an egg or some animals
shell.ex: The egg has a hard white shell.

get.ex: I get a present on my birthday.

feed.d: to give food to a person or an animal
feed.ex: I feed my fish every morning.

hatch.d: to come out of an egg
hatch.ex: The baby turtle hatches from its egg.

lab.d: a room where scientists do tests
lab.ex: We wear goggles in the lab.

communicate.d: to share ideas with others by talking, writing or moving
communicate.ex: We communicate with our hands and faces too.

act.d: act out: to show a story with your body, like in a play
act.ex: We act out the story of a butterfly.

stage.d: one part of how something grows or changes
stage.ex: A tadpole is one stage of a frog's life.

find.d: to see something you were looking for
find.ex: I found my lost shoe under the bed!

mate.d: an animal's partner that has babies with it
mate.ex: The swan swims with its mate.

own.d: belonging to you and nobody else

hen.ex: The hen sits on her eggs.

female.d: a girl or a woman; an animal that can be a mother
female.ex: A female lion is called a lioness.

diagram.d: a simple picture that shows the parts of something or how it works
diagram.ex: The diagram shows the parts of a flower.

fact.ex: It is a fact that ice is cold.

month.d: about four weeks; there are 12 in a year

born.d: be born: to come into the world as a baby
born.ex: My baby brother was born today.

take.d: to need an amount of time
take.ex: It takes ten minutes to walk to school.

butterfly.d: an insect with big, colorful wings
butterfly.ex: A butterfly sits on a flower.

caterpillar.d: a small long animal like a worm that becomes a butterfly

look_like.d: to seem the same as someone or something

call.d: to give a name to someone or something

eat.d: to put food in your mouth and swallow it

plant.d: a living thing that grows in soil and has leaves
plant.ex: My plant needs water every day.

stop.d: to not move or not do something anymore
stop.ex: The car stops at the red light.

move.d: to go from one place to another

skin.d: the outside cover of a body

become.ex: A little girl can become a teacher.

hard.d: not soft; difficult to bend or break

soon.d: in a short time from now

come.d: come out: to go from inside to outside
come.ex: The sun comes out after the rain.

young_adj.ex: The young bat stays close to its mother.

think.d: to use your mind to have an idea

talk.ex: I talk with my friend at lunch.

write.d: to put words on paper with a pencil or pen
write.ex: I write in my journal every day.

predict.d: to say what you think will happen
predict.ex: I predict it will rain today.

social_studies.d: a school subject about people, places and how we live together
social_studies.ex: In social studies we learn about maps.

link.ex: This story has a link to our science lesson.

research.d: to look for facts about something
research.ex: I research animals in library books.

long.ex: How long can you hold your breath?

live.d: to have your home in a place

chart.d: a picture with boxes or lines that shows facts
chart.ex: We made a chart of our favorite fruits.

put.d: to move something to a place
put.ex: Put your toys in the box.

order.d: the way things are put: first, next, last
order.ex: Put the blocks in order from small to big.

science.d: learning about the world by watching and testing
science.ex: In science we look at bugs and plants.

meet.d: to see someone and say hello for the first time

nancy_simmons.ex: Nancy Simmons learns about bats all over the world.

scientist.d: a person who studies the world and does tests
scientist.ex: The scientist looks into a microscope.

amnh.d: a very big science museum in New York City, with dinosaurs and animals
amnh.ex: You can see a giant whale at the American Museum of Natural History.

study.d: to learn about something by reading and looking carefully
study.ex: My sister studies for her test.

bat.d: a small animal with wings that flies at night

world.d: the Earth and all the people and places on it
world.ex: There are many countries in the world.

kind.d: a group of things that are alike in some way
kind.ex: There are many kinds of apples.

forest.d: a big place with lots of trees

hold.d: to have something in your hands or arms

false_vampire_bat.d: a big bat with very big ears; it eats bugs, frogs and mice
false_vampire_bat.ex: A false vampire bat hunts at night.

large.ex: An elephant is a large animal.

time.d: at a time: one after another, not all together
time.ex: Walk up the stairs one at a time.

pup.d: a baby bat; also a baby dog or seal
pup.ex: The pup holds on to its mother.

hair.d: the soft, thin things that grow on your head and body

stay.d: to keep being in a place or a way
stay.ex: Stay close to me in the store.

safe.ex: The baby bird is safe in its nest.

hang.d: to hold on to something from above
hang.ex: The monkey hangs from a branch.

few.ex: There are a few cookies left.

fly.d: to move through the air with wings

leave.d: to go away from a place or person

upside_down.d: with the top at the bottom

happen.d: to take place; to come about
happen.ex: A fun thing happened at school today.
